prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which established the basis for incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: one prize part on B022 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 showed that all six of us rest the case on the same science, namely a continuous line from human incretin physiology and proglucagon-derived peptide biology to the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and then to receptor agonists with independently confirmed effects on glycaemia, body weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. Nothing in the exchange raised a maturity objection. I considered a two-part prize, but with a three-person ceiling it would cut B022 to two names and leave out a contributor to the discovery line itself to make room for a second achievement that no member ranks above it. The single-part configuration is the one I can defend on exact credit.
statement.case_against: The attribution weaknesses named by every member remain real and I have not resolved them. Habener is outside the credited names, Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested, and Knudsen's engineering of liraglutide and semaglutide is excluded by the cap. A purely physiological citation can be read as honouring the hormone and not the medicine, and Nobel practice rarely offers a second chance. I have not checked priority dates and cannot do so from the materials allowed at this stage. If the committee were to conclude that Mojsov's standing cannot be supported, the trio would need to be reconsidered rather than defended by default.

responses.point: Perlmann said Mojsov's inclusion rests on a disputed priority question that cannot be settled from the ballots, and asked whether she should be named over Knudsen or other early contributors.
responses.response: I take this as the most serious challenge to the trio, and I have not moved on it because of numbers. My reason for keeping Mojsov is that the case I can verify from the supplied evidence is that she identified and synthesized the active truncated peptide, and that step is what made rational receptor-agonist design possible. Naming Knudsen instead would change the citation from discovery to drug development, which is a different prize. I agree with you that the priority dispute is unresolved, and I would not claim otherwise. If the committee's own reading of the dossier undermined her standing, I would want the citation reworded around physiology and the proglucagon-derived peptides rather than quietly replacing her.

responses.point: Sandberg argued that Knudsen's drug design is more naturally recognised separately from a discovery prize and that a discovery-only configuration is cleaner.
responses.response: I accept that the discovery framing is cleaner and I keep it. I still disagree that the exclusion is costless, because a separate recognition is not something this committee can promise. Where I part from you is on the remedy. The honest option is to say plainly in the citation that the prize is for the physiology and the active peptide, and to treat Knudsen's omission as a consequence of the three-person ceiling and not as a judgement that her work is lesser. I do not think a second prize part for drug development is justified when it would require removing a named discoverer from B022.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius asked whether a second distinct achievement such as CAR-T should share the prize with GLP-1, given the three-person cap and the strength of the GLP-1 case, and said she regards the physiological discovery as separable from later drug engineering.
responses.response: I agree that the physiology is separable from the drug engineering, and that is what I want the citation to say. On the second part, my answer this round is no. A June and Sadelain CAR-T part would take two of three places and leave B022 with one name, which cannot credit the discovery line. CAR-T also still lacks the original chimeric-receptor concept in its credited names, which Perlmann and El Manira also flagged. I therefore keep B003 as my first alternative, in the June and Sadelain form, and not as a co-prize.

responses.point: The chair gave B050 as the cleaner two-person fallback if the GLP-1 allocation were judged too contested, accepting its more indirect medical impact, and kept B006 as a further alternative.
responses.response: I agree that Mori and Walter is the cleanest allocation on the shortlist, which is why B050 remains my second alternative. But I would not treat a contested GLP-1 allocation as a reason to switch to a candidate whose clinical link is indirect. The contest concerns who within the same discovery line should be named, not whether the discovery is real. I also keep B006 off my list. Hall is the essential name, but the allocation around him is unsettled and the process concerns raised by colleagues are undocumented in the round-1 files, so I cannot weigh them.

responses.point: El Manira ranked the unfolded protein response above optogenetics because of its clean two-person attribution, accepted that its medical impact is indirect, and noted that the mammalian UPR branches lie outside the credited names.
responses.response: I agree with the ordering of B050 over optogenetics, for the reason you give: six credited names in B034 cannot be reduced to three without dropping a decisive contributor. I also take your point on the mammalian UPR branches. Mori and Walter's discovery of the signalling principle is a defensible core, but the later PERK and ATF6 work means the citation would have to be written narrowly. That, together with the indirect clinical payoff, is why I keep B050 as an alternative and not a co-prize.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide withstands the dossier, and whether Habener's absence makes the trio unsafe; I have not verified chronology.
Whether the committee will accept Knudsen's omission as a consequence of the three-person ceiling, given that no second chance is likely.
Whether the original chimeric-receptor concept can be acknowledged fairly in any B003 citation.
How to weigh the indirect clinical impact of B050 against demonstrated therapeutic impact if B022 had to be reconsidered.
statement.conflict_note: No change. I co-authored the 2016 Science spatial transcriptomics paper and have eight recorded co-authored works with Rickard Sandberg (count not audited); Sandberg has disclosed the same. None involves a credited name on any shortlisted ballot, and shared institutional affiliation is not treated as a conflict. I recuse from nothing.
